Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module one on molecular spectroscopy and in today's class we are going to look at electromagnetic spectrum and the information obtained from each region of the spectrum.

Key details

  • Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation, which is divided into different regions based on the frequency of the radiation.
  • Though these demarcations are made, the boundaries are not very precise.
  • Then we have infrared radiation, then we have the visible region, then we go on to ultraviolet region.
  • Then more energetic X rays and finally the gamma rays which are high energetic.
  • First, the lowest energy beam, that is the radio frequency region.
  • The wavelength is ten meters to one centimeter.
  • That clearly conveys that the energy of this radiation is very low.
  • It is known as NMR and ESR.
  • NMR stands for nuclear magnetic resonance and ESR stands for electron spin resonance.
  • Electron spin resonance is also referred to as electron paramagnetic resonance sometimes.
  • What exactly do happens when radio frequency region light falls onto the sample.
  • In the case of NMR that is called that is nuclear magnetic resonance there's going to be nuclear spin reversal, whereas in the case of ESR there's going to be electron spin reversal.
  • We will start with electron spin because that is something you already understand that we can have two spins that is plus half and minus half.
  • And both of them occupy the same orbital.
  • So that means they are degenerate.
  • Both these spins, plus and minus half, are degenerate and they occupy the same orbital.
  • But in the presence of magnetic field, what happens is these will split into two levels one will be the lower level that is say minus half and the other one will be plus half.
  • What is the difference?
  • Say in one case it is the spin is clockwise and in the other case the spin is anti-clockwise.
  • When you have a magnetic field, when these electrons are placed in a magnetic field, we find that while the energy levels now split into one with lower energy and one with higher energy, it is basically.
  • How did this happen?
  • Because the electron is spinning and it interacts with the magnetic field.
  • One could be aligned with the magnetic field, the other could be opposite in direction to the magnetic field.
  • Therefore, we get two energy levels now.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us see what is the information we obtain from the different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
